instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Rub the 1 tbsp butter around the inside of two 8 by 4 inch loaf pans.
Grate the 2 zucchini on the large holes of a box grater. Don't squeeze out the liquid. That should be about 3 cups.
Whisk the 3 cups flour, 1 1/2 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp salt and 2 tsp cinnamon together in a medium bowl.
In a large bowl, whisk the 3 eggs, 1 cup oil, 1 1/2 cups sugar and 1 tbsp vanilla for about 1 minute, until smooth and well blended.
Add the flour mixture and stir with a spatula until you can't see any dry flour. The batter will be very thick. Stop as soon as it comes together, or the loaves will come out tough.
Roughly chop the 1 cup walnuts. Fold the zucchini and the walnuts into the batter. It will look stiff at first and loosen as you fold.

Divide the batter between the two pans and smooth the tops. Bake for 50 to 60 minutes, until a toothpick pushed into the center comes out clean or with a few moist crumbs. Start checking at 50 minutes.
Cool the loaves in the pans for 10 to 15 minutes. Turn them out onto a wire rack and let them cool completely before slicing. This makes 2 loaves, about 20 slices.
Wrapped well, the loaves keep on the counter for 3 days. You can also freeze one for up to 3 months.
method_notes: All three whisk the dry ingredients with cinnamon, beat eggs with sugar, fat and vanilla, fold in about 2 to 3 cups of unsqueezed grated zucchini and nuts, and bake two 8 by 4 inch loaves for 50 to 65 minutes. Natasha's Kitchen (the lead) uses a cup of light oil, 3 cups of zucchini and both baking powder and soda at 350°F. Once Upon a Chef uses melted butter, nutmeg and a little more sugar and bakes lower, at 325°F. Spend with Pennies cuts the flour to 2 cups, uses only baking soda and a full tablespoon of cinnamon. This follows the lead, which makes 2 loaves.
